body: **36 of the official questions in Linear functions are this one** — 30 Easy, 5 Medium, 1 Hard.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- You get a fully defined function with no unknown constants and a single input value, and you're asked for the output.
- The wrong choices are often the outputs for nearby or related inputs.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Put the given input in for x, keeping parentheses around negatives and fractions.
- 3) Check that your number is the output, not the input or some other value from the problem.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: Type the function exactly as given, then type f(value) on a new line to get the result instantly.
This is useful for fractions and negatives.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You substitute into the wrong place or drop a negative sign.
The trap is also that you solve f(x) = value when the question asks for f(value), or the reverse.
